# State-Management Requirements Checklist: ART-008 slice 2 — Artifact Freshness

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements governing this slice's one piece of
state — the relationship between the `Feedback Sweep Log` and the artifacts
directory's last commit — are complete, unambiguous, internally consistent, and
consistent with the shipped ART-007 and Phase 7 contracts this slice reuses
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command. It
tests the *requirements*, not the implementation: every item asks whether
something is written down well, never whether code behaves.

## Scoping

The workflow prompt supplied the focus areas directly, so the three contextual
clarifying questions were resolved from it rather than asked:

- **Q1 Scope breadth** → The state of `specs/<feature>/artifacts/` relative to
  the `Feedback Sweep Log` across runs: the join's ordering facts, the commit
  set permitted to move the directory, re-selection's effect on the page set,
  and convergence. Failure-report wording is out of scope — `error-handling.md`
  owns it. Slice 1 sweep internals are out of scope (spec §Out of Scope).
- **Q2 Depth** → Standard, weighted to the four focus bullets, with idempotence
  weighted above the rest per the prompt.
- **Q3 Audience/timing** → Reviewer, at the pre-implementation gate.

Items already settled by `error-handling.md` are cited to the closing
requirement and not re-litigated.

## Requirement Completeness — The Join's Inputs

- [x] CHK001 - Are requirements defined for every input the freshness decision
  consumes, each with a stated origin (read from the workflow file versus
  supplied as observation data)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-004a]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the set of `Feedback Sweep Log` cells this slice reads
  enumerated, including the cells it never reads? [Completeness,
  data-model §1]
- [x] CHK003 - Is the history the join runs against specified — local branch
  rather than remote — so a committed-but-unpushed artifacts commit has a
  stated effect on the next run's verdict? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019a]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the observation's encoding specified for the FR-007a case, in
  which a row resolves but `last_artifacts_commit` is null? The ancestry record
  rules `is_ancestor_of_artifacts_commit` "`null` when `resolved` is false"
  (data-model §2) and says nothing about the resolved-true-with-null-commit
  pairing, so FR-031's fixtures have no stated value to pin.
  [Gap, closed by FR-007b]
- [x] CHK005 - Is "joinable" defined? FR-007a's stale reading turns on "at least
  one joinable `amended` row" and the term appears in §FR-007a, §Edge Cases, and
  data-model §3 without a definition. Read as "matched a supplied record" an
  unresolvable row forces regeneration; read as "matched and resolved" it does
  not. [Gap, closed by FR-007b]

## Requirement Consistency — What May Move the Artifacts Directory

- [x] CHK014 - Is there a requirement that the dedicated regeneration commit is
  the **only** commit permitted to stage a path under
  `specs/<feature>/artifacts/`? §FR-019 makes it separate from the sweep's
  bookkeeping commit and data-model §7 gives the other two shapes a
  workflow-file-only path set, but Phase 7's own terminal commit is
  `git add -A && git commit -m "feat(SPEC-XXX): implement phase"`
  (`speckit-pro/skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution.md:2219`),
  which runs on the proceed leg after the sweep and stages anything the sweep
  left uncommitted under that directory. Nothing scopes it.
  [Gap, closed by FR-018a]
- [x] CHK015 - Do §FR-018's "leaves the artifacts directory unmoved" and the
  reused machinery's write-then-verify-then-delete cycle agree about the
  **working tree**, not only about the commit? The machinery writes each page
  directly to `specs/<feature>/artifacts/` (`phase-execution.md:924`) and
  deletes every written page that fails verification
  (`phase-execution.md:937-938`), while §FR-011 makes those writes whole-file,
  so a pre-existing page is overwritten and then deleted. On the every-page-gap
  path §FR-018 names, the directory therefore ends materially changed with no
  commit taken. [Conflict, closed by FR-018a]
- [x] CHK016 - Does §FR-037's "entirely unmoved" cover the machinery's own
  verification deletion, or only the two spec-authored removals it names
  (FR-012b's per-page deletion and FR-012's deselection removal)? A whole-set
  gap reached through an agent that wrote pages and then died
  (`phase-execution.md:919-920`) still passes those pages through the
  verification deletion, so SC-001's stated exception — "FR-012b deliberately
  leaves the previous set in place" — is not guaranteed on that path.
  [Gap, closed by FR-018a]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the deselection removal withheld on the **every-page-gap**
  path the way §FR-037 withholds it on the whole-set path? §FR-018 asserts the
  directory is unmoved on both paths, but §FR-037's withholding sentence
  governs the whole-set gap alone, so the two zero-generated paths are
  specified differently for the same obligation. [Gap, closed by FR-018a]
- [x] CHK018 - Are the three commit shapes stated as mutually exclusive, each
  with its staged path set and its trigger, and with an explicit statement that
  none absorbs another? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-019, §FR-020, §FR-039,
  data-model §7]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the empty-commit case excluded, so the join cannot be moved by
  a commit that records nothing? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, data-model §7]
- [x] CHK020 - Is the record commit's path set stated narrowly enough that it
  cannot move the artifacts directory's last-touched commit? [Consistency,
  Spec §FR-039, data-model §7]
- [x] CHK021 - Is the rationale for the dedicated commit stated as the thing
  that makes the join exact, rather than left as a convention? [Clarity,
  Spec §FR-019]

- [x] CHK029 - Are requirements defined for pages on disk with no commit ever

## Second Pass — Gaps The Remediation Itself Opened

- [x] CHK042 - Is FR-018a's "only commit that stages the artifacts directory"
  **scoped**, or does it contradict a shipped commit? First-pass FR-018a stated
  the exclusivity without a scope, which read backward onto the plan-stage
  boundary commit — a commit that legitimately carries the first artifact
  generation through its own `specs/` path set, in a sequence marked "plan
  stage only" (`phase-execution.md:788-805`, heading at `:761`). Closed by
  scoping the rule to the sweep onward and naming that sequence as untouched.
  [Conflict, closed by FR-018a]
- [x] CHK043 - Does FR-018a's restoration outcome **reopen** §FR-024's closed
  page-outcome vocabulary? FR-024 fixes three values — `generated`, `gap`,
  `removed` — and first-pass FR-018a required reporting a restoration "as its
  own outcome", which reads as a fourth. Closed by placing the restoration as a
  run-level line in the what-already-landed part beside FR-025's commit sha,
  and stating that a restored page's own outcome remains the `gap` that
  explains why it was not regenerated. [Ambiguity, closed by FR-018a]

## Remediation Log

| Item(s) | Root defect | Requirement change |
|---|---|---|
| CHK004, CHK005 | FR-007a's stale reading turns on an undefined term, and the observation has no stated encoding for the case it governs. Two readings of "joinable" produce different verdicts on the same observation, and FR-031's fixtures have no value to pin. | **New FR-007b**: defines a joinable row as one whose cell matched a supplied record with `resolved: true`, and pins `is_ancestor_of_artifacts_commit` to `false` when `last_artifacts_commit` is null. |
| CHK014, CHK015, CHK016, CHK017, CHK030 | "Leaves the artifacts directory unmoved" was asserted about the **commit** while the reused machinery mutates the **working tree** before any commit decision is made. On every zero-generated path the directory can end changed or empty with no commit taken, and Phase 7's terminal `git add -A` then sweeps those uncommitted changes into a commit touching `artifacts/`, moving the FR-001 join. | **New FR-018a**: states the working-tree obligation on every no-commit path and the invariant that FR-018's commit is the only one permitted to stage a path under the artifacts directory. |
| CHK042 | First-pass FR-018a stated its exclusivity rule unscoped, contradicting the shipped plan-stage boundary commit. | **FR-018a** scoped to the sweep onward, naming the plan-stage sequence as untouched. |
| CHK043 | First-pass FR-018a's "report as its own outcome" read as a fourth member of FR-024's closed three-value page vocabulary. | **FR-018a** places the restoration as a run-level line beside FR-025's commit sha; the page's own outcome stays `gap`. |

## Notes

- **The five items closed by FR-018a share one root defect and go to
  consensus together.** The requirement-level obligation is not in doubt: a
  guarantee about a directory has to bind the working tree, because the
  reused machinery writes and deletes there before the commit decision exists.
  What is genuinely open is the mechanism, and at least three are defensible —
  restoring the directory to its last-committed content, excluding the path
  from the sweep-up commit, or snapshotting before the dispatch and replaying.
  FR-018a states the obligation and the observable evidence and leaves the
  mechanism to Plan, but the choice changes what lands in the repository on a
  failure path, so it is surfaced rather than settled here. Routed
  `[codebase, spec]`.
- **CHK004/CHK005 (FR-007b) are not routed.** The disambiguation follows
  directly from FR-006, which already makes an unresolvable row undeterminable
  rather than stale-proving; reading "joinable" the other way would contradict
  it. Confidence is high and no second perspective would change the answer.
- Items settled by `error-handling.md` — FR-012b's deletion, FR-015a/b/d's
  ordering, FR-034a's unreachable statuses, FR-037's unmoved path, FR-038's
  commit-keyed retry, FR-039's record commit — are cited to their closing
  requirement and pass here without re-argument.
- All evidence is repo-local. Every line citation was read from
  `speckit-pro/skills/speckit-autopilot/references/phase-execution.md` in this
  worktree rather than carried over from the plan's existing cites.
